vo: Piece one: the head. A Chief Brain.
Create a new Bot, pick a face, and name it Chief Brain.
Then send it one clear message. You are the head of my team. Four Bots will report to you. Build a board that shows each Bot, its job, and its routine.
It builds a command board for two sample businesses: Driftwood Supply, a small online gear store, and Brightlane, a tiny marketing agency.
Before you move on, test it. Ask the Chief what each Bot does. If the board is wrong, fix the message, not the board.
Every weekday at eight, it reads the newest report from each Bot and writes a one-page morning brief.
And if one Bot goes quiet, the Chief notices. A missing report gets a question, not a silent gap in your morning.
Piece two: the left arm. The Store Bot.
Store Bot gets its own clear message: you look after Driftwood Supply. Track every product, how much is left, and how fast it sells.
It tracks twelve products: how much stock is left, how many sell each week, and anything that runs out in under two weeks is flagged in red.
It also shows the top three sellers, and writes fresh descriptions for the three slowest products, so they get a second chance.
Every morning at seven it refreshes the page and leaves a short summary for the Chief.
And this is the shift. You are not building a helper. You are building a system.
Piece three: the right arm. The Client Bot, for agencies.
Its message: you are the Client Bot for Brightlane. List our six clients, the keywords we track, and where each one ranks this week and last week.
Now you see the movement at a glance. Up is green, down is red, and nobody spends a Sunday evening building spreadsheets.
It keeps a report card for six clients: what went up, what went down, and the next three jobs, in plain English. Every Monday at nine.
Piece four: the chest. The Content Bot, because everything feeds into it.
Its message: plan content for both businesses, using what the other Bots found this week. Real problems make the best posts.
Every Sunday evening it plans next week for both businesses: five short video ideas with hooks, three carousel outlines, and one blog post.
Every video idea comes with a hook already written, so you never start from a blank page again.
It saves the plan for the Chief. It never posts anything on its own.
Piece five: the legs. The Lead Bot.
Its message: find ten small businesses that could use Brightlane, and look for the biggest gap in what they show online.
It builds a list of ten leads, scores each one hot, warm or cold, and writes a short first message for the hottest ones.
Hot leads go to the top of a simple pipeline, warm ones get a follow-up date, and cold ones simply wait.
Drafts only. Nothing leaves without you.
Which brings us to piece six: the shield.
Grok Bot has approvals built in. A Bot proposes the action, and anything sensitive waits for your OK.
So write the boundary in plain words: always ask me before anything goes to a customer.
Add two more while you're there: never spend money, and never delete anything, without asking you first.
That's the whole body built: six pieces, five Bots, and one set of rules. Now let's switch it on, and watch the team actually work together.
